narrative.overview:
Sociotechnic is a product console for the owner supervising coding agents in local repositories. Its slate surfaces, blue actions, compact labels, and readable evidence keep the current run and the next human decision legible. Color-coded views, prominent measurements, and expandable numbered sequences make the console more expressive without replacing its established identity. The existing console and the owner's React scaffold establish this visual language; this document records that implementation.

Runtime CSS remains canonical (Model B). `sociotechnic/ui/web/src/index.css` owns the base theme and local font loading; `sociotechnic/ui/web/src/experience.css` owns the added view accents, measurement hierarchy, and layout refinements; `sociotechnic/ui/web/src/components/ui/button.tsx` owns button variants. The frontmatter mirrors accepted values. `PRODUCT.md` supplies product context, and `sociotechnic/CONTRACTS.md` remains the behavioral authority. Surface-specific composition belongs in `sociotechnic/ui/web/.impeccable/surfaces/sociotechnic-ui-web-src-app-tsx.md`.
keyCharacteristics: Slate surfaces and blue actions, with cyan, violet, and amber view accents in system light and dark themes.
Compact evidence with direct access to original records.
Sans text for reading; monospace for paths, commits, logs, and structured records.
Flat sections, tonal evidence surfaces, clear dividers, and elevated modal dialogs.
Large tabular numerals and expandable sequences with explicit measurement labels.

rules.name: The Semantic Color Rule
rules.body: Use primary for actions and current workflow stages, positive for supported success, amber for attention, and destructive for errors or destructive controls. View accents identify context. Keep every status and measurement meaning in text as well as color.

rules.name: The Reading Role Rule
rules.body: Use Geist for prose and interface labels. Reserve monospace for technical values and structured records.

rules.name: The Flat Surface Rule
rules.body: Separate ordinary content with spacing, borders, and muted fills. Reserve the large shadow and dimmed backdrop for modal dialogs.

rules.name: The Measured Progress Rule
rules.body: A meter represents its labeled count, deadline budget, or relative reported cost. Workflow milestones and plan numbering never establish a percentage complete, acceptance, or publication.

dos: Do resolve theme colors through the existing CSS variables.
Do pair status color with explicit status text and expose missing evidence plainly.
Do preserve keyboard focus outlines and modal focus restoration.
Do keep technical details and original records accessible through progressive disclosure.
Do keep fonts and assets local.
Do label counts, deadline budgets, and relative-cost bars with their actual meaning.
donts: Don't substitute a new brand palette or display font for the existing console language.
Don't turn a passed check or gate into a claim that the human has accepted or published the branch.
Don't apply the modal shadow to every evidence section.
Don't invent completion for numbered plan steps or treat missing usage as zero.
Don't replace the intentional native project and status selects with custom listboxes without a concrete requirement.
